sonnet.problem: Card 4 quotes 'My Spirit will not contend with man forever…' and cuts off just before 'for he is mortal'. The blank then asks for the very next word of that line. The wrong answers 'proud' and 'restless' fit equally well, so a baker can only guess the wording, not reason it out from earlier cards.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'Then comes one word: however.' In verse 6:8 the word comes after the name ('Noah, however, found favor'), not as a standalone word right after the blotting-out. The description of the text is inaccurate.
sonnet.rule: Noticing: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.
